newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metal sector try for new regional deal.
newsitem.headline: German metal sector try for new regional deal.

text.p: The IG Metall trade union and employers in Germany's metal and engineering sector have agreed to hold further regional talks aimed at resolving the pay dispute across the industry, IG Metall said on Friday.

Speaking after the collapse of talks between the two sides in the southern state of Baden-Wuerttemberg, a union spokeswoman said they had now agreed to start talks on November 19 in the steel-producing region of North-Rhine Westphalia.
She added the talks would cover a range of issues, including the proposed sick pay cuts that are at the heart of the worker protests currently hitting metal and engineering firms.

The dispute over a proposed 20 percent cut to sick pay entitlements and planned reductions to other benefits was referred to regional negotiations after national talks between the union and employers failed in October.
There are hopes that regional negotiators in the state can come up with a deal that can be used as a "pilot agreement" for a national solution.
North Rhine-Westphalia is, in terms of numbers employed, the most important region for the German metal industry.
